question.leadin: Answer the following about the Edo period.
question.text: This is the modern-day name of the city of Edo, for which the Edo period was named. It is also the modern-day capital of Japan.
question.clue: The Treaty of Amity and Commerce was signed on a ship in the bay of this city, and the capital of the Showa period was this city.

swap.leadin: This emperor gave the "Jewel Voice Broadcast" to announce his country's surrender in World War II.
swap.text: Name this emperor of an Asian country that fought against the US in the Pacific Theatre of World War II.
swap.clue: The League of Blood supported greater autonomy for this man, whose most famous Prime Minister was executed after surviving self-inflicted gunshot wounds to the chest.

question.leadin: This work depicts three fishing boats swept up in the title object near present-day Yokohama. --.
question.text: Name this Hokusai print depicting Mount Fuji in the background.
question.answerHtml: The <u>Great Wave off Kanagawa</u> (or <u>Kanagawa-oki</u> <u>nami</u> <u>ura</u>; or <u>Under the Wave off Kanagawa</u>)
question.clue: This woodblock print by Hokusai that depicts three fishing boats caught in the title phenomenon near the title location while traveling back towards Edo.

swap.text: The battle for this island, home to three Japanese air fields, saw the raising of an American flag on top of its Mount Suribachi.
swap.clue: During this battle, Tadamichi Kuribayashi prohibited banzai charges and instead created a system of tunnels inspired by his tactics at the Battle of Peleliu.

question.text: During the Battle of Leyte [LAY-tee] Gulf, the USS St. Lo was the first warship sunk by one of these Japanese suicide attacks. The term means "divine wind."
question.clue: The first recorded one struck off the coast of New Guinea and they were more effective than their underwater counterparts called "heaven shifter" or kaiten.

swap.text: This man was the son of the Meiji Emperor and Showa's father. His poor health allowed the Imperial Diet to assert greater control over the government.
swap.clue: This ruler, who ceded regency power to his son due to psychological problems. His country sent a list of twenty-one demands to a neighbor.

question.leadin: Prior to both of these events, the islands of Tsushima and Iki were captured.
question.text: Name these events which occurred following Kublai Khan's conquest of the Goryeo kingdom. The first was repulsed at the Battle of Bun'ei after landings at Hakata Bay.
question.answerHtml: Mongol invasions of Japan [or Yuan invasions of Japan; prompt on invasions of Japan with “by whom?”]
question.clue: During one of these conflicts, an exaggerated 142,000-strong army was defeated at the battle of Hakata Bay.

swap.text: The Diet gained significant power under this emperor, who took power after the death of the Meiji emperor.
swap.clue: His reign saw the issuance of the 21 demands to China, though he was forced to step down in favor of his son because he was unable to complete his official duties.

question.leadin: One World Heritage site in this city was originally designed by the Czech architect, Jan Letzel.
question.text: The Enola Gay dropped Little Boy on what city, the first target of an atomic bomb in history?
question.clue: A bell with the phrase "know yourself" commemorates an incident in this city that created the first hibakusha ("HEE-ba-KOO-sha").

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the period after the disintegration of the Ashikaga Shogunate.
swap.text: The Shogunate collapsed during the Onin war between the clans Hosokawa and Yamana, marking the beginning of this period. This period included the overthrow of Ashikaga Yoshiaki by Oda Nobunaga following his conquest of Kyoto.
swap.clue: First, name this Japanese historical period in which central power was weaker than under the shogunates.

question.leadin: Identify the following about a nation's history.
question.text: During the Muromachi period this clan held the shogunate. Members included Takauji and Yoshimitsu.
question.clue: A ruler of this family promoted the "Higashiyama culture" of the eastern hills, which popularized shoin ("sho-een") homes with tatami floors; his aesthetic was exemplified by the "wabi-sabi" style of a temple that he couldn't afford to coat in silver.

swap.leadin: During this period, emperors who retired to monasteries retained power in the system of cloistered rule.
swap.text: Name this period that succeeded the Nara Period. This period came to an end with the Genpei War.
swap.clue: Starting in this period, proprietors called ryoke would hand money to government inspectors to preserve the tax-free status of their sh¯oen estates.

question.text: The importance placed on the renunciation of imperial divinity is noted in this 1999 book by John W. Dover that explores the occupation and democratization of Japan after World War II.

swap.leadin: Name these dudes from Asian history who founded dynasties.
swap.text: After the Taira clan was defeated in the Battle of Dannoura, ending the Genpei War, this man became the first shogun of the Kamakura dynasty.
swap.clue: This man seduced the daughter of his warden after he was banished to Izu for twenty years when his father tried to remove Taira Kiyomori in the Heiji Disturbance.

question.leadin: Identify these clans integral to the course of Japanese history.
question.text: The positions of Sesho and Kampaku were held during the Heian period primarily be members of this clan, establishing its namesake "Regency." Its greatest leader, Michinaga, spent several decades running Japan while locking Imperial family members in small, windowless rooms.
question.clue: The temple at Kofuku-ji was patronized by this clan, and this clan's leadership was fought over by Yorinaga and Tadamichi during the Heiji Disturbance.

swap.leadin: It took place during a period of weakness in the Ashikaga shogunate.
swap.text: Identify this Muromachi era civil war, which saw the central parties fighting intermittently from 1467 to 1477.
swap.clue: As a result of this conflict, the Hosokawa Clan became de-facto rulers of Japan.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Japanese clans that were thorns in the sides of the Great Unifiers.
question.text: This first unifier of Japan almost died when an Azai clan samurai charged his tent at the Battle of Anegawa. A Japanese poem says that "[this man] pounded the rice / Hideyoshi baked the cake / and Tokugawa ate it."

swap.text: With the Asuka Period, the Kofun Period forms part of this period of Japanese history when the imperial capital was at Nara. This period shares its name with Japan's primary ethnic group and with the Japanese battleship that was the country's flagship for most of World War Two.

question.leadin: One of these structures is named after the Japanese word for chopsticks, Hashihaka, due to its resemblance to those utensils, and is thought to contain the body of the mythical queen Pimiko.
question.text: Name these keyhole-shaped megalithic tombs in Japan. The era lasting from roughly the 3rd century to the 6th century is named for them.
question.clue: A scholarly debate centers on whether two objects with raised left arms found in one of these places depict horse herders or dancers.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Empress Saimi, who reigned from 642 to 645 AD if we are to believe the historical record.
swap.text: That data appears in this chronicle, which like the Kojiki, is semi-mythical. The first petrochemical oil spill in ancient literature appears in this text's chronicle of Emperor Tenji.
swap.clue: This set of chronicles, the most comprehensive text available for scholarship on Ancient Japan. It was completed under the supervision of Prince Toneri and presented to Empress Gensho in the year 720.
